## 2. Configuration

You must run the code below to check, and if necessary download and load, the
packages needed for the exercises.

```{r, message=FALSE}
source("funs.R")

verifier_packages(c("tidyverse", "glmnet", "tuneR", "phonTools", "umap", "dtw", "udpipe", "readtextgrid", "stringi"))
```

The code below configures the parameters needed for our work.

```{r, message=FALSE}
options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)
theme_set(theme_minimal())
Sys.setenv(LANG = "en")
```

`quantile` is another function often applied inside `summarise`. You provide a
`probs` argument, which is a number between 0 and 1. The result is the value
below which `probs` percent of the data fall and above which `1-probs` percent
fall. For example, `quantile(f1, probs=0.5)` gives the same result as the
`median()` function. In the code below, create a table with a column `f1_q1`
giving the 0.25 quantile for each IPA symbol.


## 16. LLM

Load the data with the code below and create the objects `X`, `df_meta`,
`ind_train`, and `ind_valid`.

```{r}
llm <- read_csv2("donnees/polarity_llm.csv.bz2")
llm

X <- parse |>
  mutate(lemma = stri_trans_tolower(lemma)) |>
  group_by(lemma) |>
  filter(n() > 200) |>
  to_sparse(doc_id, lemma)
df_meta <- tibble(doc_id = as.numeric(rownames(X))) |>
  left_join(meta, by = "doc_id")
ind_train <- sort(sample(seq_len(nrow(X)), 10000))
ind_valid <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(X)), ind_train)
```

Create a predictive model for the `certain` values.

```{r}

```


## 19. Text Alignment

Load the data with the code below and create a table `tg_mots`.

```{r}
tg <- read_textgrid(
  "donnees/rhapsodie/tg/Rhap-D0001-Pro.TextGrid",
  encoding="UTF-8"
)
tg_mots <- tg |>
  filter(tier_name == "words") |>
  filter(text != "_") |>
  select(text, xmin, xmax)
```
